sourceSemantics.anchor: right_bottom at clicked position; facing equals player horizontal direction
sourceSemantics.placement: All four cells must be within build height and world border, replaceable with the placement context, unobstructed and permitted by mayUseItemAt.
sourceSemantics.removal: Remove only same type, facing and expected part at the other three positions, without extra drops. Do not remove another table with mismatched orientation or part.
sourceSemantics.collision: Full selection cube, solid top slab y=12..16; no tabletop inventory.

findings: BlockItemBehavior.place creates a rollback list containing only the anchor BlockState. Its protected placeBlock override can append snapshots, but the caller discards its boolean result.

BlockPlaceEvent and CustomBlockPlaceEvent run before behavior.placeMultiState; a four-cell implementation only in placeMultiState would place secondary cells outside the default event/rollback window.
placeMultiState receives native world,pos,state,placer,item. It returns void; normal return continues with block entity load and item consumption.
Default placement fires BlockPlaceEvent rather than BlockMultiPlaceEvent. A four-cell item should present all snapshots to protection listeners.

The existing PlacedMealItemBehavior already has a separate transaction with per-cell snapshots, controller identity capture, attempted-place events, BlockMultiPlaceEvent, custom events, functions, final source-item validation and rollback.

That meal implementation is not directly reusable as an edible controller for this table: table source has no food portions or inventory. Its transaction structure is the closer implementation precedent.

Meal placement currently uses Bukkit isReplaceable and anchor collision validation; eight-immortals implementation must also account for source per-cell contextual replaceability, border, obstruction and use permissions. Do not silently inherit missing checks.

requiredRegressionScenarios: All four facings and every part invert to the same anchor.
Reject blocked, unloaded, foreign-region, out-of-height or out-of-border cells before writes and before item debit.
Recheck protection and ownership after every event callback; rollback only cells still owned by this attempt.
Any failed write, cancellation or held-item change preserves source item and restores owned previous states.
Removal/explosion involving several parts yields at most one table item, preserves unrelated replacements, and cleans up matching remote parts safely.
Creative destruction, reload, unloaded neighbors and Folia boundaries need explicit lifecycle behavior.
